conclusion: A catch-all external rewrite is not proven to work unchanged. It must preserve the browser-visible authority for same-origin checks or perform strict trusted-origin normalization at the proxy. Configured public-origin and Google host-only nonce contracts remain separate obstacles to full transparent dual-domain operation.

findings.conditional_reproduction: Host=upstream Railway, Origin=Vercel =>403, including X-Forwarded-Host and Forwarded. Host=Vercel/Origin=Vercel =>200. Actual Vercel upstream Host was not queried by this task.
findings.evidence: panel_auth._same_origin compares parsed Origin.netloc exactly to Host; forwarded headers are ignored. Login and every cookie-auth mutation call it.
__Host-orion_session is Secure+HttpOnly+SameSiteStrict+Path=/ with no Domain. Server stores only SHA256(session token) in existing Redis; domain is not in claims.
findings.implication: Rewriting Set-Cookie unchanged can create a new host-only Vercel session while keeping existing Railway sessions intact. Existing Railway cookies cannot automatically travel to the unrelated vercel.app hostname; a fresh login there is required. Never weaken to Domain or SameSite=None merely to copy sessions.

findings.evidence: panel.html api/publicAuth/uploadImage uses relative URLs, credentials same-origin and X-Orion-CSRF for authenticated mutations; publicAuth login has no CSRF token yet. orion-public.js also uses relative API paths and same-origin credentials for preview.
findings.implication: Serve HTML, assets, auth and browser API on one visible origin. A static frontend making direct credentialed cross-origin browser calls to Railway is not compatible with current cookie/CORS/origin policy.

findings.evidence: The landing contact POST requires Origin == configured PANEL_PUBLIC_URL, independently of incoming Host; public booking POST calls _same_origin. No forwarded-browser-header trust fallback.
findings.implication: Preserving Host alone cannot make a new-domain contact form work while PANEL_PUBLIC_URL remains the Railway origin. A reviewed canonical-origin or trusted proxy-normalization strategy is needed.

findings.evidence: GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI must share origin with PANEL_PUBLIC_URL. Google connect requires request.url.netloc equal callback.netloc, then sets host-only Secure/HttpOnly/Lax nonce at /integrations/google/callback. Callback requires that exact browser nonce before provider exchange.
findings.implication: Starting from a Vercel cookie origin and returning to the current Railway callback loses the nonce and fails403; Host-preserving new-origin connect with old callback fails503. Full Google transparency cannot be claimed without canonical callback/provider configuration and preserving the existing Railway flow, or an explicitly separate Railway entry point. Do not rewrite provider redirect_uri strings or weaken nonce checks as a shortcut.

findings.evidence: Email public URLs and booking/invitation links are generated from PANEL_PUBLIC_URL. Explicit /conectar-whatsapp and OAuth callback_result redirects are relative; automatic FastAPI slash redirects use received Host/scheme.
findings.implication: /panel/ can redirect the browser to upstream Railway if Host is upstream; preserve or narrowly remap same-upstream Location at the proxy. An Origin/Host strategy does not automatically migrate email/public links. Keep all existing provider URLs/credentials intact until separately reviewed.

findings.evidence: /panel and login/logout have no-store; authenticated /auth/me currently returns csrf and identity without a Cache-Control response header. Client fetch(cache=no-store) alone is not a server/CDN cache policy. No application CORSMiddleware was found.
findings.implication: Proxy must guarantee private/no-store for auth, authenticated API, panel and preview responses, pass distinct Set-Cookie headers faithfully, and avoid logging cookies/Authorization/CSRF or OAuth code/state query values.

findings.evidence: Media image upload accepts8*1024*1024bytes; generated media <=1500000bytes. Audio ingress accepts2000000bytes and120s content duration, with30s processing scope. Public landing includes mp4/FileResponse assets. UI currently polls HTTP; no WebSocket/EventSource usage was found in app source.
findings.implication: Any Function/middleware/proxy choice must be checked against official request/response size, streaming/range and duration limits. An8MiB request must not silently become unsupported. Do not retry unsafe methods automatically or strip CSRF/content/idempotency/cookie headers.

findings.evidence: Login and public form limits key off request.client.host; start_api uses uvicorn defaults without explicit proxy-header/trusted-IP arguments. Effective environment/proxy trust was not inspected here.
findings.implication: Verify safe real client-IP behavior in the deployment without enabling arbitrary forwarded-header trust; otherwise clients may share a Vercel-edge rate-limit bucket. X-Forwarded-Host alone does not affect _same_origin.

isolated_execution.browser_limit: HTTPX cookie host scoping and emitted cookie attributes were checked, not a real browser SameSite/real login or actual Vercel platform forwarding.
isolated_execution.harness_history: Two initial harness-only runs retained: missing repo pytest asyncio mode, then Windows event-loop self-pipe blocked. Final runner supplies repo config and allows only socketpair self-pipe; no source behavior was patched to pass.
isolated_execution.network_boundary: Network/DNS prohibited; only Windows asyncio socketpair self-pipe internal loopback is allowed during socketpair construction. No external/real endpoint or infrastructure started.
isolated_execution.real_code: Orion FastAPI/panel_auth/sales-origin/OAuth callback and helpers; actual password hash verification with synthetic credentials; Redis memory fake; no database.

minimal_safe_solution.before_choice: Confirm documented/preview-observed Vercel external-rewrite request Host/Origin behavior and Railway host routing. Do not count a200GET landing as authenticated panel acceptance.
minimal_safe_solution.full_no_backend_change_limit: The local tests prove the conditional backend Host/Origin/cookie contract, not an implemented proxy. A validated proxy-normalization design still needs its own tests and cannot transparently solve current Google callback/nonce or canonical public-link flows by itself. Keep those unchanged on Railway with an explicitly separate entry/acceptance, or review canonical-origin/callback configuration and official provider registration before promising full site equivalence.
minimal_safe_solution.if_pure_rewrite_cannot_preserve_contract: Use a small reviewed trusted-origin/backend adaptation or a proxy with explicit origin/redirect policy, with exact fixed-origin allowlist and regression tests. Do not disable CSRF, reflect arbitrary Origin, add wildcard credentialed CORS, expose SUPPORT_API_TOKEN in browser or migrate databases/session stores.
minimal_safe_solution.preferred_if_platform_supports_it: Use a narrowly fixed upstream origin and same-visible-origin routing for the existing site/panel/assets/auth/API, keeping all application state on Railway. If the proxy changes Host, validate incoming Origin against one exact approved Vercel origin BEFORE normalizing it to the fixed upstream origin; reject unexpected/null/ambiguous origins and do not accept user-supplied forwarded authority. Preserve cookie+CSRF checks and private no-store; rewrite only fixed-upstream absolute redirects when necessary. Use routing middleware only if official limits/header semantics meet existing body/timeout contracts; do not assume a generic Function is drop-in.
minimal_safe_solution.preservation: No migration, new native identity provisioning, QR relink/logout, IA/campaign flag change, owner secret/Redis/DB copy or provider real message is needed for serving the frontend. Railway original remains available; frontend hostname needs its own login cookie.

proposed_isolated_preview_acceptance: Observe upstream Host/Origin/scheme and forwarded headers through a disposable echo target with synthetic values before selecting rewrite semantics.
Use fake backend session/Redis and browser: login/me/logout, valid/missing/wrong CSRF, cross-origin rejection, two domains with separate host-only cookies, no token exposure.
Check absolute slash redirects and relative redirects; every private auth/API/preview response bypasses cache, Set-Cookie preserved without Domain rewrite.
Exercise representative browser GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE and complete8MiB upload/response/range/timeout contracts against synthetic services, no data or messages.
Test contact-form canonical Origin and OAuth nonce/callback domain explicitly with fake provider. Keep current Railway integration functional; do not infer it from panel GET.

Only after preview contracts pass: publish site/panel facade and verify read-only public/asset hashes and health. A fresh real admin login is a separate acceptance with the owner; no test message/campaign.
task_scope: Read-only current Orion source inspection and synthetic local ASGI contract tests. No app/repo edit, deployment, real host/Redis/DB/provider access, campaign or message. Separate Vercel platform documentation/actual rewrite behavior is owned by the orchestrator.
